findings.passage: As the District 50 Representative in the NC House, I will rise up, speak out, and, as the late John Lewis said, “get in good trouble” to protect and assure our right to the ballot and our right for representation.
findings.note: From her 2022 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answer on key campaign messages (first message: the right to vote and the right to representation). It does not mention ID or citizenship rules.

Listed among the No votes on the House vote to override the Governor's veto of S747, Elections Law Changes. The bill text includes photo-ID cross references (G.S. 163-166.16) alongside observer, same-day registration and other changes, so it is election law in general rather than a voter ID bill alone.
subjects: voter ID at the polls (cross references only)

findings.passage: the right to vote and the right to representation: The state should assure that all eligible voters have unhindered access to the ballot—i.e., no photo ID, fairly drawn districts.
findings.note: In her answer to INDY Week's 2022 general-election questionnaire (the page is dated 2022-10-20), she lists the right to vote as a top issue and gives "no photo ID" as an example of unhindered ballot access.

findings.passage: Members of the NCGA should enact legislation that encourages voting by all eligible voters, facilitates voter registration, and assures access to the ballot by all people. We need to thwart all attempts at voter intimidation and voter suppression.
findings.note: In her answer to INDY Week's 2022 primary questionnaire (page dated 2022-04-27), she says the legislature should encourage voting, ease registration and assure ballot access, and should stop voter intimidation and suppression. It does not name photo ID.
NC House, Third Reading (roll call #810), 2024-12-11: nay (tally 73–45); census gate: none.
subjects: photo ID for all voters (constitutional amendment, in person and by mail)
